The instrument is often used at meshrep gatherings. Silk thread wound round the neck forms the frets, the outermost string plays the melody and the rest act as drone and sympathetic strings. Beginners first check that the bridge sits on the skin and is held by the tension of the strings, then tune the three melody strings in fourths with two or three drone strings and the sympathetic strings, and practise stopping frets and plucking.

熱瓦甫具有溫暖而富有穿透力的音色，音質兼具明亮與暗沉的特質。其音域寬廣，從低沉渾: The rubab has a warm, carrying timbre, both bright and dark in quality. Its range is wide, from a deep, full bass to a clear, sharp treble, and it is especially good at delicate phrases in the middle register. Its resonance comes mainly from the wooden soundbox, which gives the sound warmth and good projection. Compared with the soft refinement of the Western lute, the rubab is more penetrating and more distinctly local; compared with the pipa it is warmer rather than sharper. Plucking produces rich overtones and harmonic resonance, and the colour moves between brilliance and calm, with strong expressive power that brings out the deep character of Central Asian music.

The Seni rubab of North India can be hung from the shoulder and played while walking, the Kabul rubab is bowed, and the Central and South Asian versions are plucked. In the Sikh tradition it once accompanied Guru Nanak's hymn singing.
熱瓦甫的早期紀錄見於十世紀阿拉伯文獻，亨利·喬治·法默指出其名rabab；後以r: The earliest record of the rubab appears in tenth-century Arabic sources, and Henry George Farmer notes its name rabab; it later spread in variants such as rubab and rebab through West Asia, Central Asia, South Asia and Southeast Asia. Old Persian books and Sufi poets mention it, and it is played in Khorasan in Afghanistan, in Pakistan, Iran, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Xinjiang, Kashmir and the Punjab. A fourteenth-century history of musicians records its origin in Kashgar in southern Xinjiang, and in the Qing dynasty it was listed among the music of the Hui region. It is one of Afghanistan's national instruments and the ancestor of the North Indian sarod; in early Sikh tradition it accompanied Bhai Mardana, and in 2024 the craft of making it was inscribed on the intangible cultural heritage list.

The rubab (also robab) is a string instrument of Central Asian origin, H-S number 321.321-6, a plucked instrument resembling the lute. The body is carved from a single block of wood, the hemispherical soundbox is covered with goat skin or another animal skin, the neck is slender and the fingerboard has wound-string frets; it carries melody strings, drone strings and sympathetic strings. In Central and South Asia it is mostly plucked, while the Kabul type in Afghanistan is bowed. It is Afghanistan's national instrument, played in Pakistan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran, Turkey, Iraq, Azerbaijan, Xinjiang in China and in Jammu and Kashmir and the Punjab, used in classical music and at the meshrep and similar gatherings, and in the Qing dynasty it entered the court music of the Hui region.
琴身以整塊木頭鑿成，來源提到桑樹樹幹；共鳴箱蒙動物皮，英文來源舉山羊皮，中文來源: The body is carved from a single piece of wood, the sources mentioning the trunk of a mulberry tree; the soundbox is covered with animal skin, the English sources citing goat skin while the Chinese sources list sheepskin, donkey hide, horsehide or python skin. The bridge sits on the skin and is held by the tension of the strings. String materials include gut and nylon, and the Chinese sources also say gut was used traditionally and silk is now more common. Silk thread wound round the neck forms the frets; the materials of the other parts are not recorded.
